meta.name: GET /links -- list links, with optional tag filter

from-feature.criterion: The system shall return 200 and a JSON array from GET /links, empty when no links are stored.
The system shall order listed links most recently created first.
The system shall include every stored link in the listing, reporting a null title rather than omitting an untitled link.
If the stored links cannot be read, then the system shall return 500 and shall not return an empty array, so that a failure to read is never reported as an empty shelf.
When links are listed with a tag filter, the system shall return exactly the links carrying that tag.

context.prd-excerpt:
Feature: List saved links (slug: list-links, must-have).
As someone collecting links, I want to see what I have saved, newest first, so that I can find the thing I saved this morning without scrolling.
A GET endpoint returning every saved link as a JSON array, newest first by created_at. No pagination: the fixture's scale does not justify it, and adding it would introduce a second dimension of behaviour to verify.
Considerations (verbatim from list-links): Ordering is part of the contract, not an incidental detail, so it carries its own acceptance criterion. A test that only checks the count would pass against an implementation that returns rows in insertion order and silently breaks later.
Feature: Tag links (slug: tag-links, should-have) - the filtering half only.
Attach zero or more free-text tags to a link, and filter the list endpoint by tag.
Tags are a separate table with a many-to-many join to links, not a comma-separated string column.
Considerations (verbatim from tag-links): Tag names are matched case-sensitively. Case folding is a reasonable product decision but it is not free to verify, and leaving it explicit here stops an implementer inventing either behaviour and calling it correct.
CONSEQUENCES FOR THIS TASK: - ONE endpoint, not two. The base listing and the tag-filtered listing are the same `GET /links` route with an OPTIONAL `tag` query parameter. Do not add a second route such as `/links/by-tag/{name}` or `/tags/{name}/links`. - The path is `/links`, UNPREFIXED. Not `/api/links`. `GET /links` is the only endpoint path the PRD names verbatim, in list-links criterion 1. - NO PAGINATION. Do not add `limit`, `offset`, `page` or `per_page` parameters, and do not cap the number of rows returned. The feature rules pagination out by name. - The `?tag=` match is CASE-SENSITIVE. `Tag.name == tag` and nothing else. Never `func.lower()`, never `.ilike()`, never `COLLATE NOCASE`. `?tag=Python` must NOT match a tag stored as `python`; it returns an empty array, not every link. - list-links criterion 4 is the reason this route has a try/except at all. An empty shelf and a failure to read the shelf must never look the same to a caller.

Order is `Tag.id` ascending and stable. - `title` is `str | None`, so an untitled link serialises as `"title": null` with the key PRESENT. list-links criterion 3 is satisfied by this schema, not by route code. - `created_at` is a naive UTC datetime serialised to an ISO-8601 string with no offset.

task.objective:
Create the `GET /links` route: it returns every stored link as a JSON array ordered most recently created first, an empty array when nothing is stored, an untitled link reported with a null title rather than omitted, and - when the optional `?tag=` query parameter is given - exactly the links carrying that tag, matched case-sensitively. If the stored links cannot be read, it answers 500 with an error body, never an empty array, so that a failure to read is never reported as an empty shelf.
This is ONE route serving two features: the base listing (list-links) and the tag filter (tag-links criterion 3), unioned into a single endpoint with an optional query parameter so that the filter is not built as a second route.
This task imports `LinkResponse` from L2-001 and defines no response schema of its own. It writes exactly one non-test file, `app/api/list_links.py`, and mounts nothing - L4-001 includes the router on the application.

requirements.requirement:
Create `app/api/list_links.py` with exactly this content:
"""GET /links - list stored links, newest first, optionally filtered by tag."""
import logging
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, Query, status from sqlalchemy import select from sqlalchemy.exc import SQLAlchemyError from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
from app.database import get_db from app.models import Link, LinkTag, Tag from app.schemas.link import LinkResponse
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
router = APIRouter()
@router.get("/links", response_model=list[LinkResponse]) def list_links( tag: str | None = Query(default=None), db: Session = Depends(get_db), ) -> list[Link]: """Return every stored link, newest first, narrowed to one tag when asked.""" statement = select(Link) if tag is not None: statement = ( statement .join(LinkTag, LinkTag.link_id == Link.id) .join(Tag, Tag.id == LinkTag.tag_id) .where(Tag.name == tag) ) statement = statement.order_by(Link.created_at.desc(), Link.id.desc()) try: links = db.execute(statement).scalars().all() except SQLAlchemyError as error: logger.exception("failed to read stored links") raise HTTPException( status_code=status.HTTP_500_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, detail="stored links could not be read", ) from error return list(links)
Decisions embedded above that must be preserved exactly as written:
- The path is `"/links"` with NO prefix, and the module-level router name is `router`. L4-001 imports it as `from app.api.list_links import router as list_links_router` and mounts it with a bare `app.include_router(...)`, so the path written here is the path the application serves. Do not pass `prefix=` or `tags=` to `APIRouter()`.
- ONE route. The tag filter is the optional `tag` query parameter on this same route, not a second route. Do not add `/links/by-tag/{name}` or anything like it.
- `tag: str | None = Query(default=None)`. Absent means "no filter"; present means "filter to this exact name". `?tag=` with an EMPTY value is a filter on the empty string, which matches no tag (tag names are NOT NULL and no test stores an empty name), so it correctly returns an empty array rather than every link. Do not coerce an empty string to None.
- The filter is `Tag.name == tag`. CASE-SENSITIVE, exactly as the feature states. Do NOT write `func.lower(Tag.name) == tag.lower()`, `Tag.name.ilike(tag)`, or any `COLLATE NOCASE` clause. `?tag=Python` against a tag stored as `python` must return `[]`.
- The join is written explicitly through `LinkTag`, because L1-003 declared the association ONE-WAY on `Link.tags` and `Tag` has no `.links` attribute. This is the exact statement L1-003's test 9 already proves.
- No `.distinct()`. `tags.name` is unique and `link_tags` has a composite primary key over (link_id, tag_id), so the join yields at most one row per link and a link can never be listed twice.
- `order_by(Link.created_at.desc(), Link.id.desc())`. `created_at` is the ordering the feature guarantees; `Link.id.desc()` is a deterministic tiebreak that only matters if two rows somehow share a timestamp, and it agrees with "most recently created first" because ids ascend with insertion. Do NOT order by `id` alone - that is a proxy for the real contract and would silently break if rows were ever backdated.
- The `order_by` is applied AFTER the optional join, to one statement. Do not build two separate statements for the filtered and unfiltered cases: the ordering guarantee applies to both, and duplicating it invites the two paths to drift.
- NO pagination. No `limit`, `offset`, `skip`, `page` or `per_page` parameter, and no `.limit(...)` on the statement. The feature rules pagination out by name.
- The `try`/`except SQLAlchemyError` around `db.execute(...)` is REQUIRED by list-links criterion 4 and is the only reason it exists. Catch `SQLAlchemyError` - the base class of every SQLAlchemy failure - and re-raise as `HTTPException(500)`. Do NOT return `[]` in the handler, do NOT return `None`, and do NOT let the exception escape unhandled: an unhandled error also produces 500 in production but is re-raised by `TestClient` and cannot be asserted, and the point of the criterion is that a read failure is DISTINGUISHABLE from an empty shelf. A 500 with a `{"detail": ...}` object body is distinguishable; an empty array is not.
- `raise ... from error` preserves the original exception as the cause, and `logger.exception(...)` records the traceback. Keep both: silently swallowing the cause is what makes a read failure undiagnosable.
- `response_model=list[LinkResponse]` with the route returning `list[Link]` ORM instances. `LinkResponse` sets `from_attributes=True`, so FastAPI converts them. Do NOT build dicts by hand and do NOT define another response schema - `app/schemas/link.py` already owns it.
- `db: Session = Depends(get_db)`. Do not construct `SessionLocal()` in the route: the tests override `get_db`, and the failure-injection test patches the yielded session's `execute`.
- Do NOT call `app.include_router(...)` and do NOT import `app.main` here.
- Do NOT call `Base.metadata.create_all` anywhere.

Do NOT create or edit any other file. Specifically: do not touch `app/main.py`, `app/database.py`, `app/api/__init__.py`, `app/api/save_link.py`, `app/schemas/link.py`, any file under `app/models/`, `tests/conftest.py`, or any existing test file. Do not create `app/api/tag_links.py` or `app/schemas/tag.py` - they are L2-003's files, L2-003 is running right now in a parallel worktree, and creating them here would collide in the merge queue. Do not add `app/schemas/__init__.py`.
Do not create a migration - this project has no migration tool, the schema is created from `Base.metadata`. Do not run `git init` and do not touch `.git`.

task.test-requirements:
Test-driven: write `tests/test_list_links.py` FIRST, run `python -m pytest tests/test_list_links.py -v` and watch it fail with ModuleNotFoundError on `app.api.list_links`, then write `app/api/list_links.py` until it passes.
Every test below carries `covers` AND `from-feature`, because this task descends from two features whose criterion ids collide. `covers="3" from-feature="list-links"` and `covers="3" from-feature="tag-links"` are two different requirements.
PATTERN NOTE. list-links criteria 1, 2 and 3 are `ubiquitous`: each asserts an INVARIANT that must hold after EVERY operation, not one outcome after one action. Tests 2, 3 and 4 are therefore written as loops that re-check the property after each successive insert. A single "insert two links, list once" assertion would be a state-driven test and would pass against an implementation that only happens to be right for two rows.

Every fixture row below is created with `Link(...)`, `Tag(...)` and `link.tags.append(tag)` directly on `db_session`.
Test: test_the_listing_is_always_200_and_a_json_array - INVARIANT test: at every point in a link's lifetime, and with or without a filter, GET /links answers 200 and a JSON array. - Request the `api` and `db_session` fixtures - Define a local helper: def listing(**params) -> list: response = api.get("/links", params=params) assert response.status_code == 200, (params, response.status_code) body = response.json() assert isinstance(body, list), (params, type(body)) return body - With nothing stored: Assert listing() == [] (empty array, not null, not an object) Assert listing(tag="python") == [] (a filter on an empty shelf is still []) - Now insert three links one at a time, and after EACH insert re-check the invariant: for index in range(3): db_session.add(Link(url=f"https://example.com/{index}")) db_session.commit() assert len(listing()) == index + 1 assert listing(tag="python") == [] (still no tags attached anywhere) - After the loop, delete every link and check the invariant holds on the way back down: for link in db_session.execute(select(Link)).scalars().all(): db_session.delete(link) db_session.commit() Assert listing() == []
Test: test_links_are_always_ordered_most_recently_created_first - INVARIANT test: after every insert, the whole listing is in newest-first order - not just after the last one. - Request the `api` and `db_session` fixtures - inserted: list[str] = [] - for index in range(4): link = Link(url=f"https://example.com/{index}") db_session.add(link) db_session.commit() inserted.append(link.url) body = api.get("/links").json() # newest first == the reverse of the order they were inserted in assert [item["url"] for item in body] == list(reversed(inserted)), index # and the timestamps themselves are non-increasing down the array stamps = [datetime.fromisoformat(item["created_at"]) for item in body] assert stamps == sorted(stamps, reverse=True), index - After the loop assert len(inserted) == 4, so the loop provably ran. - Note on why this is deterministic: `Link.created_at` is assigned by Python at INSERT with MICROSECOND resolution (L1-001's decision), so four links created inside one second still carry four distinct, increasing timestamps.
Test: test_every_stored_link_is_listed_and_an_untitled_one_reports_a_null_title - INVARIANT test: after every insert, EVERY stored link is present, and an untitled link is present with `"title": null` rather than being omitted or given a substitute. - Request the `api` and `db_session` fixtures - rows = [ ("https://example.com/a", "Titled A"), ("https://example.com/b", None), ("https://example.com/c", "Titled C"), ("https://example.com/d", None), ] - for index, (url, title) in enumerate(rows): db_session.add(Link(url=url, title=title)) db_session.commit() body = api.get("/links").json() stored = db_session.execute(select(Link)).scalars().all() # nothing is omitted: the listing and the table agree, every time assert len(body) == len(stored) == index + 1, index assert {item["url"] for item in body} == {row.url for row in stored}, index by_url = {item["url"]: item for item in body} for row in stored: item = by_url[row.url] assert "title" in item, (index, row.url) # the key is never dropped assert item["title"] == row.title, (index, row.url) - After the loop, assert the two untitled links are reported as JSON null specifically: body = api.get("/links").json() by_url = {item["url"]: item for item in body} Assert by_url["https://example.com/b"]["title"] is None Assert by_url["https://example.com/d"]["title"] is None Assert by_url["https://example.com/a"]["title"] == "Titled A"
Test: test_a_failure_to_read_returns_500_and_never_an_empty_array - This is the negative case criterion 4 states: the stored links cannot be read, so 500 and NOT an empty array. Provoke the read failure rather than inventing a different one. - Request the `api`, `db_session` and `monkeypatch` fixtures - First establish that the shelf is NOT empty, so an empty array in the failure case could not be mistaken for a truthful answer: db_session.add(Link(url="https://example.com/a", title="Example A")) db_session.commit() Assert len(api.get("/links").json()) == 1 - Now make the read fail. The route calls `db.execute(statement)` on the session the dependency override yields, which is the `db_session` object itself: def boom(*args, **kwargs): raise SQLAlchemyError("the shelf could not be read")
monkeypatch.setattr(db_session, "execute", boom) - response = api.get("/links") - Assert response.status_code == 500 - body = response.json() - Assert body != [] (the whole point: a read failure is not an empty shelf) - Assert isinstance(body, dict) - Assert body["detail"] == "stored links could not be read" - Assert the same holds for the filtered listing, which runs through the same read: filtered = api.get("/links", params={"tag": "python"}) Assert filtered.status_code == 500 Assert filtered.json() != [] - `monkeypatch` restores the real `execute` at teardown, so nothing leaks into another test.
Test: test_filtering_by_tag_returns_exactly_the_links_carrying_that_tag - EVENT-DRIVEN: one action - listing with a tag filter - produces one observable outcome: exactly the links carrying that tag. - Request the `api` and `db_session` fixtures - Arrange three links and two tags, attached through the ORM: tagged_one = Link(url="https://example.com/1") tagged_two = Link(url="https://example.com/2") untagged = Link(url="https://example.com/3") python_tag = Tag(name="python") web_tag = Tag(name="web") db_session.add_all([tagged_one, tagged_two, untagged, python_tag, web_tag]) db_session.commit() tagged_one.tags.append(python_tag) tagged_two.tags.append(python_tag) tagged_two.tags.append(web_tag) db_session.commit() - The action, and its outcome: body = api.get("/links", params={"tag": "python"}).json() Assert [item["url"] for item in body] == [ "https://example.com/2", "https://example.com/1" ] (exactly the two links carrying `python`, still newest-first; the untagged link is excluded and no link appears twice) - Narrower filter: Assert [item["url"] for item in api.get("/links", params={"tag": "web"}).json()] == [ "https://example.com/2" ] - The filter does not lose the tag names in the response: body = api.get("/links", params={"tag": "web"}).json() Assert body[0]["tags"] == ["python", "web"] (ordered by Tag.id, which L1-003 fixed) - CASE-SENSITIVE, and it must return nothing rather than falling back to every link: Assert api.get("/links", params={"tag": "Python"}).json() == [] Assert api.get("/links", params={"tag": "PYTHON"}).json() == [] - An unknown tag returns nothing, not everything: Assert api.get("/links", params={"tag": "unknown"}).json() == [] - And with NO filter the untagged link is still listed, proving the filter is what excluded it and not the join: Assert len(api.get("/links").json()) == 3

# app/api/list_links.py from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, Query, status
router = APIRouter()
@router.get("/links", response_model=list[LinkResponse]) def list_links( tag: str | None = Query(default=None), db: Session = Depends(get_db), ) -> list[Link]: ...
Import as: `from app.api.list_links import router` L4-001 mounts it as: from app.api.list_links import router as list_links_router app.include_router(list_links_router)
Downstream contract: - The router carries NO prefix. Its single route is `GET /links`, and `app.include_router(router)` with no arguments serves it at exactly that path. - It is NOT mounted by this task. `app/main.py` is untouched and still serves no `/links` route; L4-001 mounts this router together with L2-001's and L2-003's. - Success is 200 with a JSON ARRAY of `LinkResponse` objects, `[]` when nothing matches. The array is never null and the response is never an object on success. - Ordering is `created_at` DESCENDING, tiebroken by `id` descending - most recently created first. It holds for the filtered listing too. - `?tag=NAME` narrows the result to exactly the links carrying a tag whose name equals NAME EXACTLY. The match is case-sensitive: `?tag=Python` does not match a tag stored as `python` and returns `[]`. An unknown name returns `[]`, never every link. Omitting the parameter returns everything. - There is NO pagination. Every matching link is returned. - Failure to read answers 500 with `{"detail": "stored links could not be read"}`. It never answers `[]` on failure, so a caller can always tell an empty shelf from a broken one. - L4-001's end-to-end test may rely on all of the above: save two links through `POST /links`, tag one through `POST /links/{id}/tags`, then assert `GET /links` returns both newest-first and `GET /links?tag=NAME` returns exactly the tagged one.
